title: Invariant-ring quotient of a stack with a finite flat affine cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, stacks in groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A finite flat affine cover of a stack $\mathcal A$ means an affine scheme $U$ and a representable surjective morphism $U\to\mathcal A$ which is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, tested after scheme base change using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal A/S$ be Deligne--Mumford and let $U\to\mathcal A$ be a finite flat affine cover. The 2-fibre product $R=U\times_{\mathcal A}U$ is an affine scheme, and its projections $s,t:R\to U$ are finite locally free: on affine charts the corresponding ring modules are finite projective. Let $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $C=\{b\in B\mid s^*b=t^*b\text{ in }\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)\}$. There are an $S$-structure on the affine scheme $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and a morphism $q:\mathcal A\to M$ whose composite with $U\to\mathcal A$ is induced by $C\hookrightarrow B$, and $q$ is uniform categorical, separated, quasi-compact, and a universal homeomorphism. A morphism $q:\mathcal A\to M$ to an algebraic space over $S$ is uniform categorical when, for every flat map $M_1\to M$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ and every algebraic space $Z/S$, composition with $q_1:\mathcal A\times_M M_1\to M_1$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(M_1,Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(\mathcal A\times_M M_1,Z)$; flatness is tested on scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. A morphism of stacks is separated when its relative diagonal is proper, with properness tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is quasi-compact when, after every scheme base change $T$ into its target, inverse images of quasi-compact opens of $T$ have quasi-compact underlying point spaces. It is a universal homeomorphism when every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism on underlying point spaces. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The underlying points are field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas.

source.place: Tags 0DUM (lemma-well-nigh-affine), 0DUP (lemma-well-nigh-affine-moduli-space), and 0DUR (lemma-moduli-space-finite-affine), with definition-categorical-quotient (Tag 0DUG). Relative S-structure obtained by unique factorization of the structure map to S.

proof.text: The etale atlas of $\mathcal A$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] makes $\mathcal A$ an fppf stack. The two maps $R=U\times_{\mathcal A}U\to U$ are scheme base changes of the finite cover: they are finite, hence affine with affine source, by the cover's scheme-test definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. They are flat and locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free] and [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective] to obtain the claimed finite projective coordinate modules. Identity, inverse and composition send isomorphisms in the 2-fibre product to identities, inverses and composites; their laws hold in each fibre groupoid [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

All maps are over $S$. Here $M$ carries the $S$-structure $\sigma$ of step 11, whose construction uses only the statements cited there and none of steps 2--10; the map $\phi:U\to M$ defined by $C\hookrightarrow B$ through [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] is then an $S$-map. An invariant map $U\to Z$ to any algebraic space $Z/S$ descends uniquely to $\mathcal A\to Z$: for $x\in\mathcal A(T)$ the scheme $P=T\times_{\mathcal A}U$ is an fppf cover of $T$, and the two maps $P\times_TP\to U$ are related by their tautological arrow in $R$. The maps $P\to Z$ therefore agree on overlaps and glue uniquely since $Z$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pullbacks and isomorphic objects give the same glued section. Conversely, a map from $\mathcal A$ restricts to an invariant map. Since $\phi s=\phi t$, $\phi$ descends to $q:\mathcal A\to M$. For an affine $S$-scheme $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$, an invariant map $U\to Z$ corresponds exactly to a ring map $D\to B$ with image in $C$, that is, to a map $M\to Z$ through which it factors; this map is over $S$ because its composite to $S$ and $\sigma$ agree after $\phi$ (step 11). Thus $q$ is categorical for affine targets. This argument works for every DM stack with such a cover.

source.place: Tags 0DUH (lemma-quotient-compare), 0DUP, first paragraph; explicit fppf gluing.

proof.text: For every flat map $C\to D$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the pulled-back cover and relation with coordinate rings $B_D=B\otimes_CD$ and $L_D=L\otimes_CD$, where $L=\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)$. The operations base change and remain finite locally free by [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-basechange-polynomial-norm]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $0\to C\to B\xrightarrow{s^*-t^*}L$. Its tensor extension identifies $D$ with the equalizer in $B_D$. Step 2 therefore proves categoricality for affine targets after each flat affine base change; the $S$-structure of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ through $M$ is that of step 11 for the base-changed groupoid, since both agree after $\operatorname{Spec}B_D\to\operatorname{Spec}D$. We use this observation for all finite-flat affine covers below; it uses no noetherian or field assumption.

source.place: Tag 03BK(3), kernel calculation in its proof; Tag 0DUP, final paragraph.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants], $B$ is integral over $C$. After an affine test $T=\operatorname{Spec}D\to M$, the map $U_T\to T$ is affine with ring $B\otimes_CD$, integral by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map]. For every algebraically closed field $K$, [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] says $U(K)\to M(K)$ is onto with fibres the $R(K)$-orbits. Every object of $\mathcal A(K)$ lifts to $U(K)$: its nonempty finite scheme of lifts has a $K$-point by [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point]. The 2-fibre product defining $R$ identifies its arrows with isomorphisms between these lifts. Hence $\pi_0\mathcal A(K)\to M(K)$ is bijective. The same statement on the fibre over each geometric point of any algebraic stack $\mathcal T\to M$ shows $|\mathcal A\times_M\mathcal T|\to|\mathcal T|$ is bijective: the target $M$ is a sheaf, so the comparison isomorphism in the fibre product is unique. Common field extension is exactly the point equivalence [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 0DUP, integral and orbit arguments; Tag 03BL. Direct geometric-fibre proof of universal bijectivity.

proof.text: For an affine $T\to M$ and a closed subset $F\subseteq|\mathcal A_T|$, its inverse image in $|U_T|$ is closed by continuity [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Its image in $T$ is closed by step 4, and equals the image of $F$ because the finite cover is surjective after base change [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus $q_T$ is closed and bijective, hence a homeomorphism. The fibre products used here are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. For an arbitrary algebraic stack $\mathcal T\to M$, choose a smooth scheme atlas and affine opens $T_i$ in it. The pullback of a closed $F\subseteq|\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}|$ to each $\mathcal A_{T_i}$ has image equal to the inverse image in $T_i$ of the image of $F$: a pair of points above a common point admits a common field extension and hence an object of the 2-fibre product. These inverse images are closed by the affine case. The atlas quotient-topology criterion [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] proves the image of $F$ closed. Along with step 4 this proves the required universal homeomorphism. Also $U_T$ is affine, hence quasi-compact, and its continuous surjection onto $\mathcal A_T$ makes $\mathcal A_T$ quasi-compact. Covering every quasi-compact open in a scheme test by finitely many affine opens gives quasi-compactness of $q$.

source.place: Tag 0DUP, universal closedness and quasi-compactness paragraphs; explicit reduction from arbitrary stack tests to affine tests.

proof.text: To check the relative diagonal of $q$, use the fppf cover $U\times_MU\to\mathcal A\times_M\mathcal A$. It is surjective flat locally finitely presented: it is the composite of two base changes of the chosen cover [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Its pullback of the diagonal is $j:R\to U\times_MU$. The projection $s:R\to U$ is finite, so proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The affine scheme $U\times_MU$ is separated over $U$; its diagonal is the closed immersion induced by multiplication of its affine coordinate algebra. Thus [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] makes $j$ proper. The diagonal $\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\times_M\mathcal A$ is representable by algebraic spaces: its base change by $(x,y)\in(\mathcal A\times_M\mathcal A)(T)$, a pair with $q(x)=q(y)$, is the sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_T(x,y)$, an algebraic space because the diagonal of $\mathcal A$ is representable. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-proper-fppf-target-test] to it to conclude $q$ separated. This same argument applies to every finite-flat affine cover.

source.place: Tag 0DUM, final paragraph (Tag 0DTY); relative diagonal proof of separatedness.

proof.text: We next prove uniqueness for arbitrary algebraic-space targets. Suppose $h_1,h_2:M\to Z$ agree after $q$. Their equalizer $E=M\times_{(h_1,h_2),Z\times Z,\Delta_Z}Z$ is a scheme: the diagonal of an algebraic space is representable by schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It is a monomorphism, and $q$ factors through $E$. After any scheme base change to $M$, the inclusion of point sets $|E_T|\to|T|$ is bijective since $q_T$ is onto, and is closed since the closed map $|q_T|$ factors through it with a surjective first map. Consequently $E\to M$ is a scheme universal homeomorphism. By [lem-trf-universally-homeomorph-integral] it is integral, hence affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so $E$ is affine. Affine categoricality from step 2 produces $r:M\to E$; uniqueness into the affine target $M$ gives $ir=1_M$. Since $i$ is a monomorphism, $ri=1_E$. Hence $E=M$ and $h_1=h_2$. The argument applies after every flat affine base change by steps 3--5.

source.place: Tag 0DUR, uniqueness paragraph; the equalizer is schematic by representability of the space diagonal.

proof.text: Let $g:\mathcal A\to Z$ and $p\in M$. Select an affine etale scheme chart $V\to Z$ and a geometric lift of the image of $p$. After a common field extension, choose an algebraically closed field $K$ and a lift $u\in U(K)$ of $p$ with image $v\in V(K)$; existence follows from step 4 and the chart's surjectivity. Put $U'=U\times_ZV$, a scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its map to $U$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], locally quasi-finite by [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite], and separated: its relative diagonal is the pullback of $\Delta_{V/Z}$, which is closed because the diagonal $\Delta_V$ of the affine scheme $V$ is closed. Define $R'=R\times_ZV$. The common $Z$-map on endpoints makes $R'\rightrightarrows U'$ a groupoid with finite locally free source and target, the base changes of $s,t$. The orbit of the chosen point $u'$ is finite: it is the target image of the finite source fibre. By [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set] it lies in an affine open of $U'$. Then [lem-sfb-locally-free-groupoid-invariant-affine] gives an invariant affine open $W\subset U'$ containing it. Set $H=(s')^{-1}W=(t')^{-1}W$; it is affine finite locally free over $W$.

source.place: Tag 0DUR, existence paragraph: Tag 07S0 followed by Tag 03JE.

proof.text: The morphism $(W,H)\to(U,R)$ has cartesian source and target squares: for example $R\times_{s,U}W$ consists of an arrow with a chosen lift in $V$ of its source; its target has the same $Z$-image and hence the same lift in $V$, and invariance of $W$ puts that target in $W$. This construction and its reverse are inverse on every scheme test. Stabilizer squares are cartesian too: a loop at $(u,v)$ is precisely a loop at $u$ together with the same $v$, since the sheaf $Z$ has only identity automorphisms. Let $D$ be the invariant ring of $(W,H)$ and $N=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-groupoid-etale-invariant-comparison]. It gives an etale $N\to M$ and $W\simeq U\times_MN$. The chosen point of $W$ shows $p$ lies in its image. The source square gives $H\simeq R\times_MN$. The $S$-structure of $N$ through $M$ is that of step 11 for $(W,H)$, since both agree after $W\to N$. The invariant map $W\to V$ factors uniquely through an $S$-map $a:N\to V$ by the ring-map calculation of step 2. Composing $a$ with $V\to Z$ yields $h_N:N\to Z$. Its composite from $W$ is the original $g$ on the pulled-back cover of $\mathcal A_N$, and the fppf sheaf gluing argument of step 2 makes $h_Nq_N=g|_{\mathcal A_N}$.

source.place: Tag 0DUR, final paragraph; Tag 0DUQ reduces to groupoids Tag 0DT9. Cartesian squares verified on test schemes.

proof.text: For every $p$ choose the preceding affine etale $N_p\to M$. The resulting set-indexed family covers $M$; size choices use [def-weil-size-convention]. On each overlap $N_p\times_MN_{p'}$, both maps to $Z$ pull back to $g$. The overlap is affine, since both $N_p,N_{p'}$ and $M$ are affine, and is flat over $M$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Step 7, with step 3, makes the two maps equal there. They therefore glue uniquely to $h:M\to Z$ by the fppf sheaf axiom [def-trf-algebraic-space]; equality $hq=g$ is checked on the pulled-back etale covering. This proves categoricality for all spaces. Everything in steps 4--10 applies to the cover pulled back to any flat affine $M'\to M$; step 3 identifies its invariant spectrum with $M'$, proving categoricality there. For a general flat algebraic-space $M_1\to M$, take an affine etale scheme cover of $M_1$ and affine covers of its overlap spaces. Each chart is flat over $M$, and the just-proved categoricality gives unique local factorizations which agree on those overlap charts. The sheaf axiom glues them uniquely. This proves uniform categoricality.

source.place: Tag 0DUR, etale gluing (omitted small detail); Tag 0DUJ, affine tests for uniform categoricality.

proof.text: $S$-structure. This step uses only the statements cited here. Let $(U,R,s,t)$ be any groupoid of $S$-schemes with $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $R=\operatorname{Spec}L$, $s,t$ finite locally free and invariant ring $C$, e.g. ours, those of step 3, or $(W,H)$ of step 9. Let $\phi:U\to M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ come from $C\subseteq B$ and $\pi:U\to S$ be the structure map, so $\pi s=\pi t$. For $f\in C$, $\phi^{-1}D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}B_f$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]; localization is flat, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] for $0\to C\to B\to L$ makes $C_f$ the equalizer of $s^*,t^*$ on $B_f$, and $C_f\to B_f$ is injective. By [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] $\phi$ is surjective and $\phi(u_0)=\phi(u_1)$ iff some $r$ has $s(r)=u_0,t(r)=u_1$; by [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants, lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map] $\phi$ is closed. (a) If $a,b:M'\to Y$, with $M'\subseteq M$ open and $Y$ a scheme, agree after $\phi$, they agree on points; for $m\in M'$ take an affine open $Y'\ni a(m)$ and $D(g)\ni m$ inside $a^{-1}Y'=b^{-1}Y'$: the ring maps $\Gamma(Y')\to C_g$ agree after $C_g\hookrightarrow B_g$, so $a=b$. (b) For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda\subseteq S$, $\pi^{-1}V$ is a union of $\phi$-fibres, so $M_V=M\setminus\phi(U\setminus\pi^{-1}V)$ is open with $\phi^{-1}M_V=\pi^{-1}V$; these cover $M$. For $D(f)\subseteq M_V$, $\Lambda\to B_f$ has equal images under $s^*,t^*$, hence factors through $C_f$, giving $D(f)\to V$ with composite $\pi$ after $\phi$. By (a) these agree on overlaps and glue to $\sigma:M\to S$ with $\sigma\phi=\pi$; $\phi$, hence $q$, is an $S$-map. The affine scheme $M$ need not be affine over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0DUP, first paragraph (invariant morphism U -> M); S-structure by Zariski gluing over affine opens of S, using groupoids.tex Tags 03BJ, 03BK, 03BL.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-38a0918a5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 0DUG, 0DUM, 0DUP, 0DUQ, 0DUR (full proofs), groupoids 0DT9, more-morphisms 07S0 and stacks-properties 04XD with its 04XB list (which includes proper). The item statement is unchanged and the item is still unsplit live; there is no re-split note and no cycle. Steps 1, 3-5, 7, 8 and 10 check out against the cited statements. Step 5's closedness argument, step 7's equaliser argument (universal homeomorphism, hence integral, hence affine, hence E=M), step 9's three cartesian squares (verified on points; U'⊂U×V because Z is a sheaf) and step 10's overlap gluing are all correct. Three repairable faults, corrected in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/. (1) C1/E1: step 2 'forgets the S-structure' and step 11 applies 'absolute categoricality' with uses=[]. That treats algebraic spaces and stacks over S as objects over Spec Z (Stacks 03I4 and 04X4), and no node carries that. Step 11 now builds sigma:M->S by Zariski gluing over affine opens V of S, citing only nodes already in proof_deps: orbit-fibres (phi surjective, fibres are orbits), integral-invariants and integral-spec-closed (phi closed, so M_V is open), flat-tensor-exact (C_f->B_f is the equaliser and injective) and morphism-into-affine. Part (a) of step 11 shows that maps agreeing after phi are equal. Step 2 now works over S throughout. Steps 3 and 9 now check that the S-structures through M agree with step 11's. (2) B2/B3: the new node lem-sfb-representable-proper-fppf-target-test said 'equivalently proper after every scheme base change … scheme properness', which makes no sense for a non-scheme space. It now defines separated, finite type and universally closed explicitly, as in lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality, and adds def-weil-closed-immersion and def-weil-finite-type-morphism to stmt_deps. (3) E5: step 6 now justifies that the relative diagonal over M is representable, via Isom_T(x,y). New nodes: the 0DT9 node matches hypotheses (1)-(4) and the conclusion (small cases checked: empty U', identity, invariant open; a subgroup inclusion fails the source square). The 07S0 node is exact. The 04XD-proper node is stack-level and not a duplicate of 0422 or the field four-property node. None of the three restates a clause of the item. Batch-5: every listed citation (def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, the stack chartwise/descent/point/fibre-product nodes, a1 etale-lqf, trf 04DF and 02X2) is general geometry, not part of the proof of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so I accept them.
